finding.summary: The G2-sky failures for E1a.3, E1a.0 and E1b come from which pixels end up in the mask, not from any change in sky brightness. Mostly this is a measurement artifact (C). Part of it is code that does not match the text (A): the 'sky' mask includes the ground below the horizon. Underneath sits a real cloud-alpha change at cloud rims (B), and that change moves toward the converged reference. (1) Sky pixel values do not change. Exposure is fixed from sun altitude with ACES (not adaptive), and the cloud-pass haze is analytic. On a shared mask (both alphas < 0.02) only a median of 1.9% of pixels differ by even one 8-bit code, and the per-pixel median ln ratio is exactly 0.0000 in 97/97 rows. What changes is the mask. Finer steps raise alpha at cloud rims (mean alpha above the horizon +0.0047, higher in 98% of rows for E1a.3). About 2.5k-9k rim pixels cross 0.02 (median alpha 0.012 in C0 -> 0.043 in E1a.x). These pixels sit 1.2-3.7x above the C0 mask median, so dropping them pulls E's median down. All 30 (E1a.3) and 35 (E1a.0) failing rows are negative. Applying E's mask to C0's own image reproduces the code's dln: corr 0.9999, max diff 0.0059 (E1a.3). With a shared mask the effect is gone: row max 0.0053 (E1a.3), 0.0163 (E1a.0), 0.0150 (E1b), with 100%, 97% and 99% of rows within 0.01. (2) The outlier ac60_e20 az s is the worst row for E1a.3 (-0.566), E1a.0 (-0.688) and also E1b (+0.153). The whole-image mask alpha<0.02 includes rows 479-583, which are the near-black ground below the horizon (alpha 0, median L 0.0038). In C0 that mask holds 37,096 sky px (median L 0.409) and 40,170 ground px, so ground is 51% of the 'sky' mask. Its median, 0.0985, falls in the gap between the two modes (p45 0.023, p55 0.130). E1a.3 loses 2,553 rim pixels, the ground share rises to 52.5%, and the median drops into the ground mode (0.0559). The ground pixels are identical in both renders (max |dL| = 0). For E1a.0 the median goes 0.0985 -> 0.0495; E1b gains 1,110 sky px and the median goes to 0.1147. With the top-78% crop the same row moves only +0.0013, and with the shared mask 0.0000. In 17/108 rows ground is at least 50% of the 'sky' mask (st90/ns100 rows 96-98%), so there the 'sky median' is a ground luminance. A/A replicas (C0 vs C0, different noise seed) already fail the code's rule: row max 0.038, 0.013 and 0.038 for the three pairs. On the code's text: §6 G2 does not state the unit or quantifier for the sky clause. The code takes the strictest reading, the max over (scene x az) rows with no az aggregation, while the cloud clause in the same sentence is per scene (median over az) with a 90% share. The mask also counts ground as 'sky', although photo_metrics' own docstring and its cf line use the top-78% crop.

finding.implicationForLaterRounds: As implemented (whole-image per-image mask including ground, max over 108 rows, fixed 0.01, no A/A floor), G2-sky measures cloud-rim alpha and noise rather than exposure or sky brightness. R4 (E4 jitter) is effectively a noise-realization change, and C0-vs-C0 seed swaps already fail at 0.013-0.038. E4 will therefore almost certainly fail G2-sky for a spurious reason. R3 (E3/E3b erosion, E3c density diag) and R5 (E5 +/- density) change rim alpha directly. They will move the per-image masks, and on the 17 rows where ground is >=50% of the 'sky' mask (ac60_e20 s, st90/ns100 rows, sc85 s ~0.47) a 1-3% change in sky-pixel count can move the median by 15-70%, so they will very likely fail spuriously as R1 did. R2 (E2a.8/E2a.6 sun-march reach, E2b sun lowpass) changes only the secondary march. View-ray alpha, and with it the masks, should stay the same, so G2-sky should see only lighting changes in near-threshold rim pixels and is less likely to fail spuriously; that is a prediction, not measured. Under the code, G2 can never pass for any arm that changes density or noise. A sky measure that isolates sky radiance, sky = both alphas < 0.02 AND above the horizon (Job.elevation() > 0, or the top-78% crop photo_metrics already documents), gives R1 row max 0.0106 / 0.0109 / 0.0033, scene-median max 0.0019 / 0.0000 / 0.0011, and A/A <= 0.0004. Even on that mask a strict per-row max still fails E1a.3 and E1a.0 by 0.0006 and 0.0009 on one row each (ci60_e3 s; ac60_e3 t). The per-row max reading of the ambiguous §6 clause stays fragile; the per-scene or >=90%-share reading matches the cloud clause. Changing any of this is a decision on the frozen ruler for the user; R1's outcome is unaffected (G8 blocks it, and E1a.0/E1b fail G2's cloud part anyway).

finding.implicationForLaterRounds:
On G5: as frozen, it is B-relative, two-sided, and has no reference-based pass rule (unlike G10 and G1c/G7). It therefore works as a 'mean image must not change visibly' guard and does not measure grain itself: a pure noise-reduction arm passes it easily (noise-only analog max |d| 0.049 vs a 0.10 tolerance). Any arm that changes the expected image will fail it, even when the change moves toward the converged reference. C0's own systematic error against the ref already exceeds the tolerance in 50% (logIQR), 65% (structMid) and 46% (perimPerArea) of F-dev units, so an arm that fully removed step bias would also fail G5.

Round by round:
- R4 (E4 jitter) should be safe on G5 and G2-cloud as long as only the noise realization changes.
- R2: E2a.x (sun-march reach) and E2b (sun lowpass) change lighting by design. The ruler itself predicts E2a.6 fails G5 on darkFrac/shadeRange, which is the intended behavior. E2a.8 and E2b will pass only if their lighting change stays under 0.10 ln in >= 90% of rows. G5 cannot tell a correction from a regression there.
- R3 (E3, E3b, E3c) and R5 (E5 +/-) change density and opacity. G5 is not record-only for density arms (only G1c/G7 are), so those arms will very likely fail G5 if their effect is visible.
- G2-cloud will additionally pick up opacity changes through the per-image inner mask.

perimPerArea is non-monotone along the path to the reference: filling gaps first lowers it, and resolving cellular gaps raises it again. It can flag a move partway toward truth as a regression.

None of this is a code-vs-text bug, so R2 runs under these rules. If the user wants guards that can adopt a bias-correcting arm, a successor ruler would need to (1) compute G2-cloud on a shared I_B∩I_E mask, which §1.5 already adopted for sigma-s units, and (2) give G5 a reference-based pass rule (|ln m_E/m_ref| <= |ln m_B/m_ref| on ref units), which in turn needs F-std refs or G5 rows on F-dev refs. R1's outcome does not change, because G8 cost blocks adoption regardless.

finding.summary:
G10: the code does what the frozen text says (RULER-grain.md:21 and grain.py:410-421, 852-887). Its noise handling also holds up. Removing grain does not lower T_band, because T is a product taken across stills, and independent noise drops out of that product. On the C0 dev replicas, T computed within one seed matches T computed across different seeds to within +0.3 to +1.3% (median), max +5%. Meanwhile 51-61% of C0's own b1_6 power is noise, and T leaves it out. Median ln(TE/TB) is positive for every arm and band (E1a.0: +0.35 b1_6_lo, +0.17 b6_16_lo). The tolerance has no A/A term (T_KEEP 0.85 fixed; nothing in calib-grain.json), but it does not need one. C0-vs-C0 runs with seeds 12345/777/4242 fail the 0.85 test in 0/54 cells for three bands and 2/54 (3.7%) for b1_6_lo. Every replica pair keeps a share of at least 0.944.

So the failures are real changes in band power, but they are not texture loss. All 19 failing cells for E1a.0 are closer to the converged reference image in that band, not farther. That includes all 7 b6_16_lo cells behind the 0.899 share: sc25 e3/e5/e8 at azimuth s, sc25_tw4 t and s, ac60_tw s, and as90_e5 t. Band-image error relative to the reference drops from 0.72-0.81 to 0.10-0.11 in the sc25 s cells, and correlation with the reference rises from 0.59-0.65 to 0.94-0.95. What E1a.0 removes there is C0's coarse-march pattern. That pattern is deterministic and the same across noise seeds. It happens to carry about the same band power as the reference (ln TR/TB -0.03 to +0.04), so any change in power counts as moving away. The rescue clause (|ln TE/TR| <= |ln TB/TR|) compares power only, and cannot see that E's content now matches the reference. For E1b, 27 of 31 failing cells are also closer to the reference. Four are genuinely, but only slightly, farther: sc85 e3/e5/e8 at azimuth t in b6_16_lo (error 0.156 -> 0.185, etc.) and ns100_e5 t in b1_6_lo. So G10 is class B, a real render change toward the reference, which the guard's scalar-power test reads as texture loss.

G8: the cost is real and matches the knob physics.
- **Source of the numbers:** fetch comes from the __cost jobs: capture.ts mode 'cost' (lines 108-131, 320-360), 16 frames, exactly one ray per texel (samples 56940 = 195x292). The guard takes the median over 36 jobs at azimuth s (23 F-dev + 13 F-std), plus bundle medians (grain.py:888-903).
- **Step ratio:** the first in-cloud step is 50 + (pss-1)*entry distance (clouds.frag:488), so fetches scale with the ratio of that first step. Predicted E1a.0 ratio at 9 deg is about 2.9 for 1.5 km layers, 6.7 for ac at 4.5 km, 12.2 for ci at 9 km. Measured is 2.2-2.6, 4.7 and 9.2. For E1a.3, predicted 1.85/2.47/2.80 against measured 1.5-1.6/1.88/2.51. That matches the pre-render predictions in RULER-grain section 1: x1.3-1.6 for E1a.3 and 2-4x for E1a.0. Halving the step roughly doubles fetches, at 0.7-1.0 of the ideal ratio.
- **Bundle T = 6.98:** this has nothing to do with twilight. Bundle T holds only two jobs, ac60_tw (4.70) and ci60_tw (9.27), and their median is their mean. The same layers outside twilight give ac60 4.64-4.71 and ci60 9.19-9.30.
- **E1b at 1.75:** this is plausible, and refine is not triggering more than designed. The refine runs once per ray: gRefState goes 0->1->2 and is never reset (cloudGenus.ts:1446-1505). Per ray, E1b adds a median of 2-4 primary media samples (95th percentile 4-8) and 5-12 sun-march steps. C0's primary march takes only 1.3-5.3 in-cloud samples per ray before it ends, so these extras double the cloud-sample cost: y x2.04, z x1.91. The forecast of x1.10-1.35 assumed longer C0 in-cloud marches. Over-triggering therefore does not explain E1b's weak grain result.

G10 is not a noise problem: A/A is clean and the estimator ignores grain. Its weak point is the reference-rescue clause, which compares scalar power. In the 6 visible failing cells (sc25_e3/e5/e8 s, ac60_tw s, sc25_tw4 t/s), E1a.0's band power is below the converged reference: ln TE/TR is -0.21, -0.25, -0.22, -0.14, -0.21 and -0.15. 1. Per-guard classification (after verdicts)

None of the failing guards is a judge-code bug.

G2-sky: measurement artifact from the metric's definition (C), with a real rim-alpha change underneath (B). The text's quantifier is ambiguous (D).
- Cause: the frozen metric uses each image's own whole-image alpha<0.02 mask, which includes the near-black ground (rows ~479-583). Ground is ≥50% of the "sky" mask in 17/108 rows. The rule is the max over 108 rows at 0.01, with no A/A floor.
- Sky pixel values do not change: the per-pixel median ln is 0.0000 in 97/97 rows.
- E1a.x thickens cloud rims toward the reference. Float near-threshold alpha error vs ref: C0 -0.0077, E1a.3 -0.0017, E1a.0 -0.0005. That pushes 2.5k-9k bright rim px out of the mask and the median drops. On ac60_e20 s it falls from the mode gap (0.0985) into the ground mode (0.0559), giving dln -0.566.
- With a shared mask (both alphas < 0.02) the row max is 0.0053 / 0.0163 / 0.0150 (E1a.3 / E1a.0 / E1b).
- C0-vs-C0 seed swaps already fail the code's rule: 0.038 / 0.013 / 0.038, failing 1-2 of 18 rows each.

- sc25 brightens for real: dln 0.08-0.19 on a shared mask.
- The per-image inner mask inflates this. sc25_e3 t is 0.231 on its own mask vs 0.033 on a shared mask. E's opaque area matches the reference to about 2%.
- E1a.3 passes the cloud part as coded (share .931, max .162); E1a.0 fails it (.862). On a shared B∩E mask: E1a.3 1.000 / .125, E1a.0 .966 / .194.

G5: real change (B).
- The expected image changes deterministically and in step with step size. Pre-resolve z-test RMS z is 3-13, against 0.95-1.14 for A/A.
- A noise-only analog passes 100% (max |d| 0.049). A/A max |ln| is 0.030 against the 0.10 tolerance.
- Direction vs the reference: toward it on cloudL (0.047 -> 0.014/0.011), logIQR (0.100 -> 0.067/0.040) and shadeRange (0.039 -> 0.024/0.020). Mixed on structMid. Away on perimPerArea (only 31-33% of units get closer). darkFrac cannot be tested (0 in every F-dev unit).

G3: for E1a.x about 2/3 artifact (C) and 1/3 real (B); for E1b mostly C.
- B=3 on ci60_e45 rests on margins of +0.12 and +0.09 logit.
- The int8 dynamic-quantized CLIP plus batch-of-3 coupling makes labels unstable: imperceptible ±1 LSB perturbations of C0 give hits=3 in only 1 of 21 draws (expected 1.95).
- Real part: the smoothed Ci margin on azimuth 'a' goes 0.85 -> -0.09 (E1a.0) and -> 0.07 (E1a.3), about 5-6 SD.

G10: real change (B), with two design gaps in the text.
- A/A is clean: minimum share 0.944, failing cells 2/54 in b1_6_lo and 0 elsewhere. T ignores grain (within-seed vs cross-seed differs by +0.3-1.3%).
- In E1a.0's failing cells, correlation with the reference rises in 19/19 (e.g. sc25_e5 s 0.59 -> 0.94). In the decisive b6_16_lo cells, though, E's band power is 13-22% below the reference, while C0's deterministic coarse-march pattern happened to sit at reference power.
- Gap 1: the rescue clause compares power only, and the reference runs with temporalUpscale off, so TB > TR in only 0-11.6% of units. The rescue is almost never reachable.
- Gap 2: there is no visibility floor. 19/69 b6_16_lo units have TB < 1 code², including the failing as90_e5 t (TB 0.046).

G8: real cost (B); the guard is sound.
- Fetch ratio follows the first-step ratio. Medians: E1a.3 1.606, E1a.0 2.603, E1b 1.752.

2. Code that does not match the frozen text

Judge logic for G2, G3, G5, G10 and G8: no mismatch. grain.py sha 0bc75131 matches the freeze list (RULER-grain.md:311).
- G2: RULER-grain.md:100 gives cf the "F-std 위 78 %" crop; :101 defines sky as "하늘(알파 < 0.02) 중앙 L" with no crop. grain.py:435 and :438 implement :101 literally.

- G3: RULER-grain.md:230 ("장면마다 맞는 방위 수 ≥ B") equals grain.py:1080 (all(E>=B)). grain.py:1075 keeps hits only and throws the margins away.

- G10: RULER-grain.md:21 equals grain.py:852-887.

- RULER-grain.md:103 defines fetchCost x as primary weather fetches ("x(1차 날씨)").
- capture.ts:110 and :124 read takram's sampleCount.x. That counter is declared `out ivec3 sampleCount` (node_modules/@takram/three-clouds/src/shaders/clouds.glsl:125) and passed in at clouds.frag:527, so every primary media sample resets it.
- Evidence: in C0 st90_e5 s, x = 0 in 100% of texels while y-z ≥ 1 everywhere. x < yp in 21-100% of C0 hit texels.
- Lower-bound corrected medians: E1a.3 1.626, E1a.0 2.682, E1b 1.806, E2a.8 1.182. No decision changes. The error is conservative for E2 arms; density arms will read slightly cheaper than they are.

3. What happens in R2-R5

Two guards fail essentially any arm that changes cloud-pass pixels, whether or not the change is an improvement.

G3:
- P(pass) for a pixel-changing but perceptually null arm is about 0.14 (smoothed model vs official B; hits=3 on ci60_e45 in 1/21 perturbations). That is roughly an 86% spurious-fail rate in every round.
- Only a byte-identical arm passes for certain.

G2-sky:
- The A/A per-row fail rate is 4/54 = 7.4% (95% lower bound about 2%).
- Over 108 rows, P(pass) ≈ 0.926^108 ≈ 2.5e-4. Even at 2% per row it is 0.98^108 ≈ 0.11.
- The failures concentrate in the 17 ground-heavy rows, where about 180 px of mask change moves the median 1.3-3.8%.
- E3, E3b, E3c, E4 and E5 change rim alpha or the noise realization, so they will almost certainly fail.
- R2: on tw1734/tw1746 the E2 arms flip 56-455 sky-mask px, and E2a.6 flips 279-455, at or above the scale that failed A/A, even though dln on those two scenes was 0.0000. E2a.6 is exposed; E2a.8 and E2b are uncertain.

Combined, assuming independence:
- R3/R4/R5 arms: P(pass G2-sky and G3) ≲ 0.11 × 0.14 ≈ 1.5% at the optimistic end, realistically well under 1%.
- R2 arms: at most about 14%.

R4 (E4 jitter): a seed swap is exactly the A/A case, so G2-sky fails almost certainly and G3 fails about 86% of the time. G5, G2-cloud and G10 should be fine (G10 exempts E4), provided the jitter distribution does not move the expected image; that is untested.

Guards that fail any arm that really changes the image, improvements included (these are not noise-driven):
- G5: A/A max 0.030 vs tolerance 0.10. It will fail the R3/R5 density arms, and any R2 arm whose lighting change exceeds 0.10 ln in more than 10% of rows. The ruler itself predicts E2a.6 fails on darkFrac/shadeRange. C0 itself is within 0.10 of the reference in only 50% / 35% / 54% of units (logIQR / structMid / perimPerArea), though this is confounded by the reference's temporalUpscale being off.
- G2-cloud: opacity changes in R3/R5 inflate it through the per-image inner mask.
- G10: E2a.8 and E2b remove the sun-march tau staircase, another deterministic pattern, so they are exposed. Four cells (cu35_e3/e5 a, sc25_e3/e5 a in b1_6_hi) failed in all three R1 arms, which leaves only 2 cells of the 6-of-69 allowance. Density arms get no rescue (grain.py:877), which is intended.
- G8: R2 passes (E2a.8 1.194 with O5 bundle 1.304; E2a.6 1.000; E2b 0.759). It stays the binding guard for step-size arms.

Net: under the frozen rules, R2-R5 will almost certainly adopt nothing, and the guards doing the blocking (G2-sky, G3) say nothing about whether an arm is better or worse.

4. Options

(a) Keep everything frozen and continue.
- Integrity cost: none.
